answer: The design leans on escrowed payment for graded work, taxed when attestations come from one subnet, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Each submission hangs on the velvet of a task receipt, and the lantern is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. The pigment of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Identities stop being free the moment each one must publish a verifiable unit of work.
